"83e64850-0509-590c-9b94-f4e62ac5f1ba" :question/id #uuid "83e64850-0509-590c-9b94-f4e62ac5f1ba"] [:db/add "83e64850-0509-590c-9b94-f4e62ac5f1ba" :question/problem "Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x-3y+3z &=12 \\ -2x+2y-4z &=-12 \\ -2y-5z &=-2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$."] [:db/add "83e64850-0509-590c-9b94-f4e62ac5f1ba" :question/worked-solution "The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -3 & 3 & 12 \\ -2 & 2 & -4 & -12 \\ 0 & -2 & -5 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & 2 & -4 & -12 \\ 0 & -2 & -5 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & -5 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & -5 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=2 \\ y &=1-\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)(2) \\ &=-4 \\ x &=4-(-1)(-4) \\ &\quad -(1)(2) \\ &=-2\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(-2,-4,2\right)
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & 2 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & -4 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4\end{array}\right]

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -3 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4\end{array}\right]

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -3\end{array}\right]

\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
\left(\frac{1}{6},-\frac{1}{3},-\frac{3}{2}\right)

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -4\end{array}\right]

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right]

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$."] ["83e64850-0509-590c-9b94-f4e62ac5f1ba" :question/worked-solution "The augmented matrix is

\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & -5 & -2\end{array}\right]

\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=2 \\ y &=1-\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)(2) \\ &=-4 \\ x &=4-(-1)(-4) \\ &\quad -(1)(2) \\ &=-2\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & 2 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & -4 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & -4 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -3 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -2 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=\frac{1}{2}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-\frac{3}{2} \\ y &=\frac{2}{3}-\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) \\ &=-\frac{1}{3} \\ x &=-1-(-1)\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) \\ &\quad -(1)\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) \\ &=\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(\frac{1}{6},-\frac{1}{3},-\frac{3}{2}\right)
$$

The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -3 & 3 & 12 \\ -2 & 2 & -4 & -12 \\ 0 & -2 & -5 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & 2 & -4 & -12 \\ 0 & -2 & -5 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & -5 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & -5 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
